answer: New standing is sponsored, not self-claimed: an established identity stakes credit on a climber's promised work, and the stake burns if the summit - the final verified output - never forms. Progress pulses from the climber must be countersigned by the sponsor, who checks what they back rather than rubber-stamping it. Each verified summit mints a pearl: a receipt naming sponsor, climber, and exact work. A farm sponsoring clones pays real credit on fake summits - every failure burns the sponsor, so a fake fleet must produce genuine summits or bankrupt itself. Honest expeditions compound.
